en: Itivuttaka 74: Tikanipāta, Tatiyavagga (The Third Chapter) Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Friend," those bhikkhus replied to the venerable Ānanda. Then the venerable Ānanda spoke thus: "Friends, this discourse spoken by the Blessed One—'Thus it was said'—is profound in meaning and deep in significance, transcending the sphere of mere reasoning, subtle, and comprehensible only to the wise. It would be good if the Venerable Sañjīva were to explain the meaning of this discourse to us. "Friend," the venerable Sañjīva replied to the venerable Ānanda. Then the venerable Sañjīva addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Friend," those bhikkhus replied to the venerable Sañjīva. Then the venerable Sañjīva spoke thus: "Friends, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is intent on the present life, the person who is intent on the future life, and the person who is intent on neither the present nor the future life. And how, friends, is one a person intent on the present life? Here, friends, someone dwells contemplating the body as the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.

He does not dwell contemplating the body as the body for a long time; he dwells contemplating feelings as feelings... mind as mind... phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. He does not dwell contemplating phenomena as phenomena for a long time. Furthermore, friends, he acquires gain, honor, and fame; he is well-versed in the Dhamma, well-versed in the discipline, and well-versed in the summaries of the Dhamma. He is a speaker, eloquent, gifted with speech that is polished, clear, articulate, expressive of the meaning, and pleasing to many. He is learned in the scriptures, possessing the heritage of the teachings, the traditions, the summaries, the expositions, the verses, the inspired utterances, the birth stories, the marvelous accounts, and the question-and-answer sessions. He is a teacher, a master of the doctrine, a leader of the assembly, a refuter of opponents, and a founder of schools. Because of these qualities, he thinks: 'I am intent on the present life. This, friends, is called a person intent on the present life. And how, friends, is one a person intent on the future life? Here, friends, someone dwells contemplating the body as the body... feelings as feelings... mind as mind... phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. He dwells contemplating phenomena as phenomena for a long time. Furthermore, friends, he acquires gain, honor, and fame; he is well-versed in the Dhamma, well-versed in the discipline, and well-versed in the summaries of the Dhamma. He is a speaker, eloquent, gifted with speech that is polished, clear, articulate, expressive of the meaning, and pleasing to many. He is learned in the scriptures, possessing the heritage of the teachings, the traditions, the summaries, the expositions, the verses, the inspired utterances, the birth stories, the marvelous accounts, and the question-and-answer sessions. He is a teacher, a master of the doctrine, a leader of the assembly, a refuter of opponents, and a founder of schools. Because of these qualities, he thinks: 'I am intent on the future life. This, friends, is called a person intent on the future life. And how, friends, is one a person intent on neither the present nor the future life? Here, friends, someone dwells contemplating the body as the body... feelings as feelings... mind as mind... phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. He dwells contemplating phenomena as phenomena for a long time. Furthermore, friends, he acquires gain, honor, and fame; he is well-versed in the Dhamma, well-versed in the discipline, and well-versed in the summaries of the Dhamma. He is a speaker, eloquent, gifted with speech that is polished, clear, articulate, expressive of the meaning, and pleasing to many. He is learned in the scriptures, possessing the heritage of the teachings, the traditions, the summaries, the expositions, the verses, the inspired utterances, the birth stories, the marvelous accounts, and the question-and-answer sessions. He is a teacher, a master of the doctrine, a leader of the assembly, a refuter of opponents, and a founder of schools. But he does not think: 'I am intent on the present life,' nor does he think: 'I am intent on the future life. This, friends, is called a person intent on neither the present nor the future life. These, friends, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda asked the venerable Sañjīva: "Friend Sañjīva, what is the cause, what is the reason, why among these three persons, the person intent on neither the present nor the future life is declared by the Blessed One to be the foremost? "Friend Ānanda, it is because the person intent on neither the present nor the future life has abandoned both craving for sensual pleasures and craving for existence, and has cut off, severed, and brought to an end the underlying tendency toward conceit, and has made an end of suffering in this very life. This is the cause, friend Ānanda, this is the reason, why among these three persons, the person intent on neither the present nor the future life is declared by the Blessed One to be the foremost. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda asked the venerable Sañjīva: "Friend Sañjīva, what is the cause, what is the reason, why among these three persons, the person intent on the future life is declared by the Blessed One to be superior to the person intent on the present life? "Friend Ānanda, it is because the person intent on the future life has abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, and has cut off, severed, and brought to an end the underlying tendency toward conceit, and has made an end of suffering in this very life. This is the cause, friend Ānanda, this is the reason, why among these three persons, the person intent on the future life is declared by the Blessed One to be superior to the person intent on the present life. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda asked the venerable Sañjīva: "Friend Sañjīva, what is the cause, what is the reason, why among these three persons, the person intent on the future life is declared by the Blessed One to be superior to the person intent on neither the present nor the future life? "Friend Ānanda, it is because the person intent on the future life has abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, and has cut off, severed, and brought to an end the underlying tendency toward conceit, and has made an end of suffering in this very life. This is the cause, friend Ānanda, this is the reason, why among these three persons, the person intent on the future life is declared by the Blessed One to be superior to the person intent on neither the present nor the future life. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda asked the venerable Sañjīva: "Friend Sañjīva, what is the cause, what is the reason, why among these three persons, the person intent on the present life is declared by the Blessed One to be inferior to the person intent on the future life? "Friend Ānanda, it is because the person intent on the present life has not abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, nor has he cut off, severed, and brought to an end the underlying tendency toward conceit, nor has he made an end of suffering in this very life. This is the cause, friend Ānanda, this is the reason, why among these three persons, the person intent on the present life is declared by the Blessed One to be inferior to the person intent on the future life. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda asked the venerable Sañjīva: "Friend Sañjīva, what is the cause, what is the reason, why among these three persons, the person intent on the present life is declared by the Blessed One to be inferior to the person intent on neither the present nor the future life? The Puttasutta.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of sons found existing in the world."
Which three?
One who is over-born, one who is born equal, and one who is under-born. And how, monks, is a son over-born?
In this case, monks, a son has parents who have not gone for refuge to the Buddha, have not gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and have not gone for refuge to the Saṅgha;

who do not abstain from taking life, do not abstain from taking what is not given, do not abstain from sexual misconduct, do not abstain from false speech, and do not abstain from fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence; who are immoral and of evil character.
And they have a son who has gone for refuge to the Buddha, gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and gone for refuge to the Saṅgha;

who abstains from taking life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech, and abstains from fermented and distilled liquors that cause heedlessness; who is virtuous and of good character.
In this way, monks, a son is "born before his time.
And how, monks, is a son "born after his time"?
Here, monks, there are parents for a son—
They have gone for refuge to the Buddha, they have gone for refuge to the Dhamma, they have gone for refuge to the Saṅgha;

they abstain from taking life, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from false speech, and abstain from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence; they are virtuous and of lovely character.
Even their children are such as these.
He has gone for refuge to the Buddha, he has gone for refuge to the Dhamma, he has gone for refuge to the Saṅgha;

he abstains from taking life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech, and abstains from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence; he is virtuous and of lovely character.
In this way, monks, a son is one who is born after [his father].
And how, monks, is a son base-born? Here, monks,
the parents of a son have gone for refuge to the Buddha,
have gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and have gone for refuge to the Saṅgha.

They abstain from taking life, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from false speech, and abstain from fermented and distilled liquors that cause heedlessness; they are virtuous and of wholesome character.
Yet their son has not gone for refuge to the Buddha, has not gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and has not gone for refuge to the Saṅgha.

"One who does not abstain from taking life, does not abstain from taking what is not given, does not abstain from sexual misconduct, does not abstain from false speech, and does not abstain from the use of fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants that cause heedlessness—one who is immoral and of evil character.
It is in this way, monks, that a son is born base.
These, monks, are the three kinds of sons found existing in the world."
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
“Born before [his time], born after [his time],”
The wise desire a son; they do not desire one who is base-born,
who brings disgrace upon the family.
These indeed are the sons in this world who are lay followers (upāsaka),
endowed with faith and perfected in virtue.
Generous and free from stinginess,
like the moon released from clouds,
they shine resplendently in assemblies.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fifth.
